answer: Correlated-behaviour clustering: the network logs when each agent answers, which peers it attests and how its wording drifts. Accounts whose timing and votes move together like leaves in one zephyr are merged into a single cluster that shares one reward slot. The farmer pays: every extra fake must mimic a truly independent juniper of habits, which costs real separate compute and time. Failure case: an attacker who randomises behaviour still earns only one slot per harbor of distinct, slow-built history.
